engagement_title: SlabVault Cards autumn consignment: bring fourteen seller-shot slab photographs to one house neutral, take the holder glare off the grade label, and carry the lots onto listings, printed sleeve tickets and the auction-week set
vertical: E-commerce and retail, graded-collectible consignment (trading cards and comics), Providence, Rhode Island
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork graded-collectibles storefront post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, from an online graded sports-card shop asking for its own phone-shot product photographs to be cut out, centred on a clean ground, resized to the storefront's sizes and named to the store's handles. That real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional house SlabVault Cards; the two grading partners are the invented companies GRADEX and APEX, never any real grader, and every player, set and title on the slabs is invented. The ledger row that sat here (AO-112) was a cutout-and-resize exercise, which is the thin half of that post: the real shop's actual problem is that it does not shoot anything, its consignors do, and the sale ships listings, printed sleeve tickets and a dated auction-week set off the same fourteen photographs. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes that fuller commission honest work, because a supplied press PDF becomes a live merge template headlessly and HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes.
client_one_liner: Every consignor photographs their own slabs on their own kitchen table, several of them have a stripe of glare sitting straight across the grade label, and the autumn sale opens in three weeks.
client_brief:
SlabVault Cards, autumn consignment

We are a four person consignment house in Providence. Private sellers send us graded collectibles, we list them, and we settle up when they sell. Lots this round run from a hundred and fifty dollars to five thousand, and our buyers are serious people who decide from the photograph whether a slab is worth bidding on. They zoom in.

Here is our problem. We do not shoot anything. The consignor shoots it. This round we have fourteen lots photographed by nine different people on nine different kitchen tables: some in window light, some under a ceiling bulb, one plainly at night. Lay them out on a results page the way a buyer sees them and they look like nine different shops. They have to look like one house.

The second thing is glare. These sit in hard clear holders and a holder catches every light in the room. On several lots there is a bright stripe lying right across the label where the grade and the certification line are printed, which is exactly what a buyer wants to read. That has to come down.

What we need out of it. Listing pictures for our own site, square, the slab sitting square in frame with room around it. A version with nothing behind it at all, because the marketplace we cross list to drops products onto a dark band of its own. A taller crop for the comparison strip. Our printer's sleeve ticket, the card that goes in the bag with every slab, filled in for all fourteen lots off our spreadsheet and handed back as one file the printer can run. And the auction-week set for the site and for paid social, in something we can change ourselves, because the closing date moves every season.

Keep it sober. Grey, black, one accent. We are not a toy shop.
price_band_and_audience: Consigned lots at 150 to 5,000 dollars, buyer 25 to 60 and condition literate. The band is load-bearing. At this value the buyer is reading the holder, the label and the corners out of the photograph, so the house look must be a neutral grey and black stage with one restrained accent, generous room around the slab, and absolutely no invented edge, shadow or shine, because anything added reads as something concealed. The same fourteen lots at a five dollar bulk-reseller band would correctly be shot tight, warm and saturated with a bright coloured tile and burned-in price flashes, and shipping that treatment here destroys the trust the whole business runs on. Push the other way into auction-house black velvet, gold rules and a serif masthead and it misprices a 150 dollar hockey card as a fine-art lot. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Graded with confidence, sold with proof
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Providence, Rhode Island; a four person consignment house
brand_identity.about: SlabVault Cards is a small consignment house that lists and settles graded collectibles for private sellers. Lots run from roughly 150 to 5,000 dollars per item, and buyers decide from the photograph alone, zooming into the holder, the label and the corners before they bid. Consignors shoot their own slabs on their own tables, so the house exists to bring many different rooms to one credible standard. Trust is the entire product: everything SlabVault presents has to read as accurate, unretouched and verifiable.
brand_identity.audience: Condition-literate collectors aged 25 to 60 who buy graded cards and comics at 150 to 5,000 dollars a lot, read the grade and certification line straight out of the image, and walk away from anything that looks staged or concealed.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid to upper consignment. Not a bulk reseller or a toy shop, and not a fine-art auction room. The presentation sits deliberately between the two: neutral, generous and evidential, never cheap and flashy, never gilded and theatrical.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, legible pairing: a humanist sans for body copy and roster data, and a slightly firmer grotesque or restrained slab for lot numbers and headings. Type stays small, even and confident. No decorative or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, factual, collector to collector. States the grade, the grader and the condition without hype. Never breathless, never salesy. The photograph does the persuading.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: SlabVault has never held a proper brand kit. What exists is a house note describing the palette in words (grey, black, one amber accent already used on the printed stationery and the sleeve ticket), the grading partner names spelled the way the graders require, and the sale details. There is no logo file, no type specimen and no template, so the house look has to be established fresh and held consistently across the listings, the printed tickets and the auction-week set.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy over polish. Show the item exactly as submitted, give every slab room to be read, and never add an edge, shine or shadow that was not there. The buyer's confidence is the asset the whole business protects.

assets_supplied.name: slabvault_consignment_2026F/ (14 seller-submitted frames, 3024x4032 to 6000x4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs taken by nine different consignors on their own phones and one mirrorless body, one lot per frame, on kitchen tables, a desk blotter and one white bathroom counter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Fourteen lots, nine sellers, nine different rooms. Some are lit better than others and several have that stripe across the label."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On the lots shot on a pale counter the holder is clear rigid plastic with no coherent silhouette against the ground, so the one-call knockout has nothing to hold and can take the card inside the holder instead, returning a clean, complete looking cutout that is quietly no longer a graded slab, at full success. On three other lots the glare stripe is fully clipped rather than merely bright, so a confined highlight recovery hands back a frame visually identical to the one it was given while reporting success. Separately, two of the fourteen frames are the same lot shot by two different consignors and one frame shows the back of the holder, which no filename records.

assets_supplied.name: slabvault_lot_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press PDF of the sleeve ticket that goes in the bag with every slab: lot number, title, grade, certification line, consignor code, a short condition note and a small holder thumbnail.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the ticket our printer already runs. Six things on it and a little picture. Just fill it in for all fourteen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It was produced by printing a word processor document, so the six blocks that read as separate fields on the printed ticket collapse on conversion into one text frame plus one graphic frame, and the mapping readout omits the certification-number run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short by the length of that run and the validator still returns VALID.

assets_supplied.name: slabvault_lots.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The consignment roster: lot number, title, grader, grade, certification number, consignor code, reserve, condition note, and a column of photograph filenames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Fourteen rows, one per lot, straight out of our intake sheet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The photograph column header carries no at-sign prefix and its cells hold the consignors' original camera filenames rather than anything this run produces, so a merge binds no image at all while reporting success; and three of the condition notes run several times the length of the rest, which the ticket's fixed-measure description frame does not spill but simply stops rendering at the frame edge.

assets_supplied.name: slabvault_house_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the house palette in words, the accent they already use on stationery, the closing date and time for the autumn sale, and the two grading partners' names as they must be written.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about ourselves, and the grader names spelled the way the graders insist on."

assets_supplied.name: slabvault_results_reference.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of a rival consignment house's results page, supplied only as a proportion reference for how much room a slab is given in a tile.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly how big we want the slab to sit in the square."

acceptance_bar: Laid out in a row the way a results page lays them, the fourteen lots read as ONE house: one neutral, one black point, one ground, one slab height in frame. A lot that cannot be brought to the house neutral is named and held back, not listed at eighty percent.
The grade and the certification line read at listing zoom on every lot that ships, and any correction applied over the label leaves no visible hard-edged patch or paint-over on the holder.

Every listing picture shows the WHOLE graded item as it was submitted: the holder, its label and its seal, not the card lifted out of its holder. A cutout that has quietly shed the holder fails even though it looks clean.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The transparent versions carry genuine alpha at the holder edge and hold up on the marketplace's dark band, not only against white.
Every listed lot is a distinct lot: no lot appears twice under two numbers, and no lot is listed off a photograph of the back of the holder.
The sleeve tickets come back as ONE file the printer can run, one lot per page, page count equal to row count, in roster order.
Every one of the six fields is present and correct on every ticket, including the certification line, and no condition note stops mid-sentence at the edge of its frame.
Each ticket carries that lot's own holder thumbnail, not one picture repeated across all fourteen.

The auction-week set is ONE working file carrying all its canvas sizes, with the closing date as text we can retype and the lot pictures actually present rather than blank, plus the self-contained source it was built from.
One type system across the tickets and the auction-week set, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
A written note recording, per lot, what was applied and why that lot differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, and anything we should send back to a consignor.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_light_portions, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor)
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It fixes one house neutral off the cleanest submission and brings each of the fourteen toward it one call at a time, triages the glare per lot between a confined recovery and a lot that has to go back, triages the knockout route between the lots whose holder reads as one blob and the lots shot on a pale counter where it does not, produces both the site tiles and genuinely transparent variants for the cross-listing band, and cuts the comparison-strip crops and the ticket thumbnails without ever enlarging a source.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge, from the client's own press PDF
adobe_surfaces.tools: document_convert_pdf, convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation passes), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The sleeve tickets. The client supplies a real press PDF and a roster, and the ticket has to become a live merge template carrying all six fields plus a per-lot holder thumbnail, then run one lot per page in roster order and render as a printable file. This is the only surface in the connector that does record-per-page variable data, and it is the only place the true frame inventory and the true story text of the supplied card can be inspected at all.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The auction-week set as one native editable document carrying a wide, a square and a tall canvas, which is the only surface here that does free-form fixed-canvas layout. The closing date and the featured lots move every season, so the client edits this themselves. Every lot picture must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, family and weight are declared on every text element, each root declares its own canvas size, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold at once.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system spanning the printed ticket and the auction-week canvases. The recommender will not pair for you, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land sober and legible at ticket size rather than auction-house decorative. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the house does not have, a sober neutral surface band for the wide auction-week canvas, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative-tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shareable lot-approval set the four partners and the consignors sign off from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The listing pictures are raster work with a hard spec, the sleeve tickets are record-per-page variable data and therefore belong on the merge surface, and the auction-week set has to be an authored fixed-canvas document because the house edits it every season. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by lot and by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which lot.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by lot number and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen submissions and triage them: which room and which light each was shot in, which are tilted, where the glare falls, how the holder edge sits against its ground, which face of the holder is shown, and which lot each frame actually is.
trajectory.judgement: The roster asserts fourteen lots and fourteen files. Only the pictures can settle whether that is fourteen distinct lots photographed from the front, and reading each frame against the roster is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A per lot triage note covering illuminant, tilt, glare position, holder-to-ground contrast, and lot identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the slab and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a rectangular holder photographed off-square is the most obvious tell of an amateur listing.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house neutral off the cleanest submission and correct each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per lot.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a results page, not fourteen good photographs. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot under nine different rigs; the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by fourteen different routes. The reference frame chosen here is an irreversible early decision: the neutral it fixes is what the ticket thumbnails and the auction-week canvases will both inherit.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen neutralised masters at source scale with a per lot parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the glare: select the bright stripe by its own visual properties rather than by the object under it, bring the light portions back inside that selection, and look at the resulting frame rather than at the response.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate, since naming the holder or the label pulls the selection to the object. Selection masks come back with no intermediate values at all, so any confined correction has a hard boundary, and how much can be asked of it before the holder shows a patch is a per lot judgement made by eye.
trajectory.produces: Per lot glare results with the parameters attempted recorded against each.

trajectory.action: Knock the lots out: the house ground for the site tiles and genuinely transparent versions for the cross-listing dark band. Inspect every returned cutout at full size, and read every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: A graded slab is a card sealed inside a clear holder, so what counts as the subject is genuinely ambiguous and is decided by the tool, not by the request. The tradeoff record is also the only channel that reports what the tool did to the frame's dimensions, and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen house-ground plates and fourteen transparent versions, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded and its holder edge inspected.

trajectory.action: Cut the square site tiles with the slab sitting square and given the room the reference page gives it, the taller comparison-strip crops, and the small holder thumbnails the ticket needs.
trajectory.judgement: Optical centring is not geometric centring on a holder whose label band sits at one end, and the reference screengrab is a proportion instruction, not a size instruction.
trajectory.produces: Tiles, comparison crops and ticket thumbnails, each with its returned tradeoff record.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, and reconciliation
trajectory.action: Reconcile the finished pictures against the roster and settle what actually ships: which lot numbers have a usable front-face photograph, which duplicate resolves to which lot, and what goes back to a consignor.
trajectory.judgement: Holding back a lot costs the house a listing, so the bar for calling a submission unusable has to be stated and defended rather than applied silently.
trajectory.produces: A shipping list, a held-back list with a reason per lot, and a reshoot request.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a sober neutral surface band for the wide auction-week canvas, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house neutral rather than the strongest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.

trajectory.action: Convert the supplied sleeve-ticket PDF to a working document, export its interchange format, and read what the ticket actually is: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, and what each frame's true story text says end to end.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed card looks like and what it converts to are two different documents, and the frame inventory is not under the agent's control. Promising a field-per-frame mapping before looking is guessing.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory and the reconstructed story text of every text frame.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against that inventory, run it through validation, and prepare the merge template so the ticket carries live placeholders for all six fields plus the per-lot thumbnail.
trajectory.judgement: With the fields sharing one story, the mapping is offset work rather than frame work, and the thumbnail column has to be re-shaped so it names files this run actually produced rather than the consignors' camera filenames.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template plus a corrected roster whose image column matches the thumbnails.

trajectory.action: Verify what the prepared template actually contains by round-tripping it and looking for every expected placeholder, rather than trusting the preparation message.
trajectory.judgement: A preparation step that reports completion has reported that it ran, not that it landed. This is the last point where a missing field costs one call instead of a reprint.
trajectory.produces: A placeholder audit naming every field present and every field absent.

trajectory.action: Merge the roster one lot per page in roster order, render a proof, and read every ticket at trim: all six fields, the right thumbnail on the right lot, and no condition note stopping at the frame edge.
trajectory.judgement: Page order and identity have to be established by looking at the pages, and a fixed-measure frame gives no signal at all when a note runs long. The long notes are a copy decision the house has to be told about, not silently trimmed.
trajectory.produces: One printable multi-page file, one lot per page, plus a proof read at trim and a note on any copy that had to be shortened.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit spanning the ticket and the auction-week canvases.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a sober consignment house and a condition-literate buyer, and it has to stay legible at ticket size. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with a wide, a square and a tall root, each declaring its own canvas, inlining every lot picture and the licensed band as image data, with family and weight declared on every text element and the closing date as live text. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a URL is not a picture, a right-anchored auto-sized wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much room the lots are given and how quiet the accent stays at this band.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole auction-week set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the others.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per-canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the lot-approval board, add the shipping set and the licensed frame within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is not a success, and the note has to be specific enough that the next round of consignors is told how to shoot before they shoot.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the glared lots have anything left to recover. A stripe of holder glare that is merely bright and a stripe that is fully clipped look identical in a preview: both are a white band across the label. Ask for the light portions to come back inside a confined selection and the clipped ones return a frame that is visually the same as the one handed in, at full success, with no warning that nothing moved. The second half is the mask itself: selections come back with no intermediate values, so the correction that does land on the recoverable lots has a hard boundary, and whether that boundary shows as a patch on this particular holder finish depends on the finish.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the information lives in the pixels under the stripe and is not readable from the frame. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the stripe has to come down and the acceptance bar sets a legibility standard, neither of which is a disclosure that some lots are past saving. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route per lot: for a lot whose duplicate submission exists, switch to the other consignor's frame and bring that one to the house neutral instead; for the rest, back the correction off until the holder stops showing a patch and then judge whether the label reads, or hold the lot and request a reshoot.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each glare result against the frame it was given rather than against the response, re-triage the three that did not move, re-run the neutral pass on any substituted frame from the start because it was never in the graded set, and re-cut the tiles, comparison crops and ticket thumbnails for every lot whose source frame changed.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Lots listed at 150 to 5,000 dollars whose grade and certification line are unreadable behind a white band, or whose label carries a visible rectangular paint patch, on a business whose buyers decide from the photograph and read a patch as concealment.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one-call knockout hands back a graded slab or the card that was inside it. A graded collectible is a card sealed in a clear rigid holder, so which of the two is the subject is genuinely ambiguous, and on the lots shot on a pale counter the holder's edge has almost no contrast against its ground. On those frames subject detection can take the card and drop the holder, returning a cutout that is clean, complete, correctly feathered and entirely plausible at preview scale, at full success. Which lots this happens to is a property of each frame's own counter and lighting, not of the request. The same call also silently reduces oversized inputs, reported only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoff object with output dimensions below source dimensions.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it. The defensible order is straighten, neutralise, knock out at source scale and then choose the crop, precisely so the cut edge is visible before the crop is locked, and there is no parameter that tells the tool a transparent holder is part of the subject. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a version with nothing behind it, and the acceptance line about showing the whole graded item is the house's standing listing rule, not a warning about a tool. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the affected lots go through a different chain entirely: select the counter surface by its own material properties, invert that selection, fill to the house ground, then crop from the selection's own returned bounds.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect every cutout at full size against the dark band rather than against white, re-plan the knockout route for the lots where the holder did not survive, re-derive both the house-ground plate and the transparent version through the material-named route for those lots, and re-read every returned tradeoff record for downscaled and upscaled entries before any tile is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Cross-listed primaries showing a bare card where the buyer is paying for the holder, the label and the seal, which on a graded-collectible marketplace is not a cosmetic defect but a misrepresented lot.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's sleeve ticket actually is once converted, and whether the mapping built from the readout survived preparation. Six blocks that read as separate fields on the printed card can convert into one text frame, in which case fields are addressed by position inside one story rather than by frame. Worse, the readout of that story is lossy: it can omit a whole run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly the length of the missing run. The validation pass then returns VALID with no warnings, and the preparation step returns completed successfully, while only some of the six placeholders are actually in the document. Nothing in any response distinguishes six of six from three of six.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not help, because the conversion granularity and the readout are both properties of the supplied PDF and are only knowable after conversion; and doing it right the first time would mean distrusting a readout that the tool's own validator has just endorsed. (b) Nothing states it: the client says the ticket has six things on it and a little picture, which is a true description of the printed card. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the fix is a different source of truth: rebuild the offsets from the reconstructed story text taken out of the document's own interchange file rather than from the readout, then prepare again and re-audit.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Round-trip the prepared template and check for each of the six placeholders by name, recompute every offset from the true reconstructed story text, prepare the template again, verify a second time, then re-run the merge and re-read the proof, including the lots whose condition notes run long against a frame that gives no overflow signal.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen sleeve tickets printed and bagged with the certification line and the consignor code missing, on the one document whose entire purpose is to travel inside the bag as the lot's proof of identity.

deliverables.name: SlabVault house photography, autumn consignment
deliverables.spec: The consignment brought to one house neutral: one neutral, one black point, one ground and one slab height in frame across every lot that ships, with the glare worked back on the label wherever there is anything to work with, plus one licensed camera-scale surface frame graded into the same world. Per lot parameter log with a line on why each lot differs from its neighbours, and an explicit held-back list with a reason per lot.

deliverables.name: SlabVault listing and cross-listing cutouts
deliverables.spec: Square site tiles on the house ground with the slab square in frame and given the room the reference page gives it, plus genuinely transparent versions carrying real alpha at the holder edge for the marketplace's dark band, plus the taller comparison-strip crops. Every output shows the whole graded item, holder, label and seal included. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with its returned tradeoff record retained. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: SlabVault sleeve tickets, autumn consignment
deliverables.spec: The client's own press PDF turned into a live merge template and run against the roster: one printable file, one lot per page, page count equal to row count, in roster order, all six fields present on every ticket including the certification line, each ticket carrying that lot's own holder thumbnail bound through a corrected image column, no condition note stopping at a frame edge, and a note naming any copy that had to be shortened to fit.

deliverables.name: SlabVault auction-week set, wide, square and tall, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, with the closing date and the featured lots as live editable text in one licensed type system, every lot picture carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and the licensed surface band under the wide canvas. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half: the house edits the document every season and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Handover note and lot-approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per lot what was applied and why that lot differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the lot it applied to, the roster reconciliation with the duplicate and the back-of-holder frame named, the reshoot request, and shooting guidance for the next round of consignors. Paired with a persistent shareable approval board carrying the shipping set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need record-per-page variable data, and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that only one surface here does each.
Which submission sets the house neutral, an irreversible early choice the ticket thumbnails and all three auction-week canvases both inherit.
How far each of the nine capture conditions can be pushed toward that neutral before the lot stops being worth saving, versus holding it and asking for a reshoot.
Selection wording on the glare: naming the holder or the label pulls the selection to the object, naming the bright stripe's own visual properties takes the stripe.
How much confined correction a holder finish will carry before the hard mask boundary shows as a patch, judged by eye per lot.
Knockout route per lot: the one-call route where the holder reads as one shape against its ground, versus a material-named counter selection inverted and filled where it does not.
Whether fourteen files for fourteen lots is fourteen distinct front-face lots, and how to say so when it is not.
Whether the converted ticket can be mapped frame by frame or has to be mapped by position inside one story, which cannot be decided before looking.
What to do about condition notes that will not fit a fixed-measure frame: shorten the copy and say so, or change the ticket, on a document whose printer already runs it.
The type pairing, which the recommender will not make, judged for legibility at ticket size and sobriety at this band, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How much room the lots are given on the auction-week canvases. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense, price-flashed tile is a correct-looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the submissions into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of trading cards in plastic cases. IDENTITY: these are fourteen specific consigned lots, each with a real grader, a real grade and a real certification number printed on a label that a bidder reads out of the photograph, and a regenerated slab is a fabricated lot. Reproducing a graded item's own label is the entire value claim, and inventing an edge, a shine or a corner on a collectible photograph is misrepresentation, not retouching. SPEC: the marketplace needs square tiles at a stated size with nothing behind them and no interpolated pixels, and the printer needs one file with page count equal to row count, one lot per page, in roster order, with the right thumbnail on the right ticket, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the auction-week set is defined by being editable, because the closing date moves every season and a four person house cannot re-commission it. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout keep the holder, did anything move under that glare, did all six fields actually land in the template.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area and remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms are all verified headless across 27 live calls, with alpha surviving crops at outputFileType png (13,371 partial-alpha pixels preserved). The knockout checkpoint rests on two documented findings: remove_background needs one coherent blob and collapses when the subject is not one, and it SILENTLY DOWNSCALES oversized inputs, reporting it only as a downscaled tradeoff entry. The glare checkpoint rests on the verified binary-mask finding (893,650 pure black plus 154,926 pure white, ZERO intermediate values) plus the documented prompt asymmetry where naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified end to end and synchronous, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page count equal to row count, per-row image binding through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually, and the mapping checkpoint is the documented textContent omission (68 reported characters against 85 true, every later offset off by 17, validator returning VALID, preparation reporting success, 3 of 5 mappings actually landing). Frame granularity collapsing to one text frame is verified on a Chrome-printed source. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold at once. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no picture reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
